newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randfontein says cannot delay job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Randfontein says cannot delay job cuts.

text.p: Randfontein Estates Gold Mining Co Ltd said on Thursday it could not delay the planned axing of up to 4,000 jobs and hoped to meet with the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) later on Thursday head off a clash over the plan.
"The mine cannot delay the retrenchments. With each day that passes, the prejudice it suffers increases, as well as the possibility of further job losses," owner JCI Ltd said in a statement.
JCI said on May 28 it planned to shed a third of Randfontein's 12,000-strong workforce and reduce tonnage throughput as part of a far-reaching restructuring at the struggling gold mine.
JCI said consultations with NUM had resulted in agreement on all issues ecept for the severance packages payable and a final list of affected employees.
It said the mine had complied with all the requirements of the Labour Relations Act and was entitled to continue with the retrenchments.
"The mine is prepared to meet with the union as a matter of urgeny to resolve this matter and hopes a meeting will take place later today," the statement said.

Randfontein produced 4,392 kg of gold in the March quarter compared to 5,100 kg in the December quarter. It plunged into a loss of 2.86 million rand, well down on the previous quarter's 43.83 million rand profit.
At the time of reporting the March quarter the mine announced that these results could lead to a further labour retructuring programme.
